hero.title: Friday
hero.lead: You land at 08:10. The rest is up to you :)

paras: I put together a few ideas for Friday, have a look if you'd find something interesting. No stress at all, also down to just wing it, but thought it may help as some inspo :-)

ask.answersNone: No picks, so we just wing it :-)

steps.title: What do you want to see?
steps.hint: Pick as many as you like.

tiles.label: Old Rome
tiles.sub: The Colosseum, the Forum, the Pantheon, Trevi

tiles.label: Rome from above
tiles.sub: Sunset from the Vittoriano roof, Castel Sant'Angelo, the Spanish Steps

tiles.label: Weirdly interesting
tiles.sub: A bone crypt, a fake dome, a trick corridor

tiles.label: Cool art
tiles.sub: St Peter's, Bernini's marble, three Caravaggios, Haring

steps.title: And food?
steps.hint: Pick as many as you like.

tiles.label: Pastries
tiles.sub: Pain au chocolat, almond croissants, a maritozzo

tiles.label: Markets and street food
tiles.sub: A food market, supplì, gelato that isn't too sweet

tiles.label: A proper lunch
tiles.sub: Fresh pasta, a hill of Roman jars, an old wine shop, grilled scamorza

tiles.label: Make pasta
tiles.sub: Fettuccine and a tiramisu with a chef, then a sit-down meal, in English

steps.title: Wander somewhere?
steps.hint: Pick as many as you like.

tiles.label: Trastevere
tiles.sub: Ivy, cobbles, laundry lines, no plan

tiles.label: Piazza Navona
tiles.sub: Campo de' Fiori and the small streets around it

tiles.label: The Aventine
tiles.sub: The Mouth of Truth, the keyhole, the orange garden

tiles.label: Coppedè
tiles.sub: A few fairytale streets around one small square

tiles.label: Monti
tiles.sub: Vintage shops like Pifebo, a fountain square, a tiny mosaic chapel

tiles.label: The Jewish Ghetto
tiles.sub: Bakeries, a turtle fountain, a palace on a Roman theatre
A headset on the real Circus Maximus, chariots race past
A cannon fires at noon under the Gianicolo terrace
Ring a convent bell to see a chapel painted like a comic strip
One easy lap of the old chariot track

arrival.title: You land
arrival.body: We leave your bag at my hostel by Termini and start from there, around 10.

bags.title: Luggage to the Airbnb
bags.body: We drop the luggage at the Airbnb in Pigneto and take a break.

dinner.title: Dinner
dinner.bodyNone: Three pizza places. Da Ivo has pasta too, in case it's a pasta day for you :D

ideas.title: Li Rioni
ideas.line: Thin, crispy Roman pizza from a wood oven, in a loud room done up like a street

ideas.title: Da Remo
ideas.line: Loud, cheap Testaccio pizza place where the pizzas come fast and there's usually a queue

ideas.title: Da Ivo
ideas.line:
An old Trastevere pizzeria open since 1962, no booking for two, and their site says a table always turns up
They have pasta too, in case it's a pasta day for you :D

options.title: Colosseum, from outside
options.line: Sold out inside for Friday, so a walk round the outside and then the free view over the Forum from the Capitol

options.title: Roman Forum and Palatine
options.line: The Roman Forum's ruins, then up the Palatine where the emperors lived, with the Circus Maximus below

options.title: Pantheon
options.line: A 1,900-year-old dome with an open hole at the top

options.title: San Clemente
options.line: Two levels under the church: a Roman house, a temple of Mithras and an underground stream

options.title: Trevi Fountain
options.line: Free to see from the street at any time, the ticket from 11:30 is only for the steps down to the basin

options.title: Under Trevi's streets
options.line: Ruins of a Roman house under an old cinema near the Trevi, with the water that feeds the fountain still running past

options.title: Caesar's cats
options.line: The ruins where Caesar was stabbed, now with a cat shelter in one corner and cats asleep on the old stones

options.title: Vittoriano roof
options.line: A lift up to the roof of the big white monument, all of Rome around and the old Forums right below, open until after sunset

options.title: Castel Sant'Angelo
options.line: An emperor's tomb turned fortress, a long ramp and some stairs up to a terrace facing St Peter's

options.title: Pincio and the Spanish Steps
options.line: Through Villa Borghese to a free terrace over Piazza del Popolo, then along to the top of the Spanish Steps and down into Piazza di Spagna

options.title: Bone crypt
options.line: Six small rooms decorated with the bones of about 3,700 people, most of them friars

options.title: The fake dome
options.line: The church never got its dome, so a painter faked one on the flat ceiling, and from the right spot on the floor it looks real

options.title: The trick corridor
options.line: A colonnade that looks 35 metres deep but is under 9, with a warrior statue at the end that's only about knee high

options.title: The 17:30 machine
options.line: At 17:30 a 17th-century machine lowers the huge altar painting, with music, and a silver statue appears behind it

options.title: Statues in a power plant
options.line: Roman marble statues between the giant black engines of an old power station

options.title: Pyramid and Keats
options.line: A quiet garden cemetery behind a Roman pyramid, where Keats is buried

options.title: Bernini at the Borghese
options.line: Bernini's marble statues: Daphne's fingers turning into leaves, David biting his lip mid-throw

options.title: St Peter's
options.line: Enormous, with Michelangelo's Pietà just inside the door and Bernini's bronze canopy under the dome

options.title: Three Caravaggios
options.line: San Luigi dei Francesi, a church near the Pantheon with three Caravaggios in one side chapel

options.title: The Doria Pamphilj palace
options.line: A palace the family still lives in: a gilded Hall of Mirrors, then Velázquez's red-faced pope next to Bernini's bust of the same man

options.title: Keith Haring
options.line: A new show in a palace off Piazza Navona: his chalk subway drawings, a motorbike he painted in Rome in 1984 and some works under blacklight

options.title: Kandinsky
options.line: About seventy of his paintings, most on loan from the Pompidou in Paris, in a palace on Piazza Venezia

options.title: Sistine Chapel
options.line: Michelangelo's ceiling, at the end of the Vatican Museums

options.title: Maritozzo
options.line: A soft bun split open and filled with whipped cream, at Regoli near Termini, a pastry shop open since 1916

options.title: Croissants at Barnum
options.line: A bakery just off Campo de' Fiori that bakes its own pain au chocolat, plus an almond croissant on some days

say.how: In Italian it's un cornetto alle mandorle (oon cor-NET-toh AHL-leh MAHN-dor-leh)

options.title: Boccione
options.line: A tiny bakery in the Ghetto with no sign, known for its burnt-top fruit cake and sour cherry and ricotta tart

options.title: Biscuit bakery
options.line: An old biscuit bakery in Trastevere with a 16-metre oven

options.title: Testaccio market
options.line: A neighbourhood market with about 100 stalls, one selling a dripping beef sandwich most people eat standing up

options.title: Supplì
options.line: Fried rice balls from Supplizio, filled with meat, tomato and mozzarella

options.title: Trapizzino
options.line: A triangle of crusty pizza bread filled with a Roman stew, like chicken cacciatora or meatballs in tomato sauce, on Piazza Trilussa

options.title: Gelateria del Teatro
options.line: Gelato on Via dei Coronari in flavours like sage and raspberry or Amalfi lemon, and whipped cream made without sugar

options.title: Lunch at Fortunata
options.line:
Fresh pasta rolled and cut by hand in the front window, just off Campo de' Fiori
The pasta comes very al dente unless you ask for it softer, and the tiramisu is good too

options.title: Lunch in a hill of pots
options.line: A Testaccio trattoria built into a hill of broken Roman jars, some of them showing behind glass in the walls

options.title: Lunch at Enoteca Corsi
options.line: A wine shop open since 1931 a few streets from the Pantheon, with Roman cooking at shared tables between the bottle shelves

options.title: Lunch at Valentino
options.line: A Monti trattoria behind the old painted sign of an ice depot and Birra Peroni, with grilled scamorza done several ways

options.title: Pasta class
options.line: A class in English with a chef: hand-rolled fettuccine and a tiramisu, then a sit-down meal of what you made

details.label: Sauce
details.text: Tomato and basil, amatriciana or cacio e pepe, made by the kitchen

details.label: Where
details.text: Via Giuseppe Zanardelli 14, by Piazza Navona

options.title: Trastevere
options.line: Small ivy-covered streets across the river for wandering, and two vintage shops on Via di San Francesco a Ripa

options.title: Piazza Navona and around
options.line: From Bernini's fountain in Piazza Navona through the small streets to Campo de' Fiori, past the Pantheon

options.title: Mouth of Truth and the keyhole
options.line: The Mouth of Truth, said to bite liars' hands, then up the hill to the keyhole with St Peter's dome framed in it and the orange garden next door

options.title: Aqueduct park
options.line: Roman aqueduct arches nearly 28 metres tall in an open park on the south-east edge of Rome

options.title: Coppedè
options.line: About forty fairytale buildings around Piazza Mincio, with an iron chandelier hanging in a stone arch and a fountain with twelve frogs

options.title: Monti
options.line: The neighbourhood between my hostel and the Colosseum, with vintage shops like Pifebo and Humana, a fountain square and a tiny mosaic chapel that isn't always open

options.title: The Jewish Ghetto
options.line: A flat loop past a Roman colonnade with a church built into it, a palace on a Roman theatre and four bronze boys pushing turtles into a fountain, and Friday is 16 October, the day in 1943 the Nazis began rounding up over a thousand of Rome's Jews here, so there may be a commemoration

options.title: Chariot race in VR
options.line: A VR headset on the real Circus Maximus track rebuilds the stands, and a chariot race goes past

options.title: Noon cannon
options.line: A loud cannon shot below the Gianicolo terrace every day at noon, and a free view over Rome at any hour

options.title: The nuns' bell
options.line: A convent chapel painted in the 1240s like a comic strip, open if the nuns answer the bell

options.title: A lap of the Circus Maximus
options.line: One easy lap of the old chariot track, about 1.5 km, with the Palatine ruins above

options.title: Vespa sidecar
options.line: A driver takes us round the old streets on a vintage Vespa with a sidecar, one of us in the sidecar and one on the back, swapping at the stops
